title: A Self-Pruning Transformer: Extreme KV-Cache Compression w/Universal Attention
content:
Computer Science > Machine Learning

Title:A Self-Pruning Transformer: Extreme KV-Cache Compression with Universal Attention
View PDF HTML (experimental)
            Abstract:The large KV-cache size of modern LLMs creates a barrier to efficient deployment. Recent work has explored replacing attention layers' RoPE positional embeddings with alternative decay-based mechanisms, which can then be used to prune KV-cache during inference. However, these decay functions have limited expressivity, and in practice devolve into sliding-window-like eviction patterns. In this work, we propose a unifying framework for complementary and novel decay mechanisms, capturing complex key statistics and interactions while preserving expressive RoPE embeddings and Softmax attention. The resulting Universal Attention is a highly expressive and end-to-end trainable architecture, whose composite decay mechanism acts as a natural, $\textit{adaptive}$ pruning criterion, removing tokens that contribute least to attention computation. Experimentally, Universal Attention achieves state-of-the-art $10\times$ compression on natural language and synthetic task data, while $\textit{improving}$ downstream performance compared to both state-of-the-art baselines and unpruned oracles. It further demonstrates superior long-context generalization with unprecedented $25\times$ compression at length 16k.

report.summary: Universal Attention, a self-pruning transformer, compresses KV-cache up to 25× while improving long-context performance by adaptively evicting low-contribution tokens.
report.background: Modern LLMs store key-value pairs for every past token during generation. As context windows reach 128k tokens or more, this KV-cache dominates GPU memory and memory bandwidth, limiting throughput and raising serving costs. Prior work replaced RoPE with decay-based mechanisms to prune the cache, but those decay functions have limited expressivity and often collapse into sliding-window eviction. This paper proposes a unifying framework for complementary decay mechanisms that preserve RoPE and softmax attention while capturing complex key statistics, enabling adaptive token pruning. The result, Universal Attention, is an end-to-end trainable architecture that treats attention contribution as a natural pruning signal.
key_points: KV-cache growth is a major deployment barrier: every generated token adds key-value tensors, so long contexts consume huge memory and bandwidth. Existing decay-based pruning methods are simple but lose expressivity, often behaving like fixed sliding windows.

Universal Attention introduces a composite decay mechanism that preserves standard RoPE embeddings and softmax attention. It unifies complementary decay functions and learns which past tokens matter, rather than applying a fixed eviction rule.

The learned decay acts as an adaptive pruning criterion, removing tokens that contribute least to attention computation. Because it is end-to-end trainable, the model can optimize both attention and pruning jointly.
Experiments report 10× KV-cache compression on natural language and synthetic tasks, while improving downstream performance compared with state-of-the-art baselines and even unpruned oracle models.
For long-context generalization, Universal Attention achieves 25× compression at 16k sequence length, suggesting the approach scales better than prior decay or eviction methods.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this could sharply reduce memory and bandwidth costs for long-context inference, making larger batch sizes, longer prompts, and cheaper serving possible. Developers may gain a drop-in architectural idea that preserves RoPE and softmax, but adopting it likely requires retraining or fine-tuning rather than inference-only patching. Regular users could see faster, cheaper assistants that handle books, codebases, and long conversations without forgetting key details. Caveats remain: results are from a paper, code and independent replication are needed, and training costs may offset inference savings. Still, it challenges the assumption that compression must trade accuracy for efficiency.
report.tools: Watch the arXiv page and alphaXiv for code release. Related open-source projects to compare include H2O, StreamingLLM, SnapKV, and PyramidKV for KV-cache eviction; vLLM and Hugging Face Transformers for serving; FlashAttention for efficient attention kernels. Use LongBench and Needle-in-a-Haystack to evaluate long-context retention.
